english.title: Fail to give notice re works for supply of water or affecting fire hydrant
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person proposing to carry out works

(A)_[for the purpose of supplying water to part of the area of a fire and rescue authority, namely **(..SPECIFY AUTHORITY..), without reasonable excuse, failed to give at least 6 weeks' notice in writing to the authority]_
(B)_[affecting a fire hydrant, without reasonable excuse, failed to give at least 7 days' notice in writing to the fire and rescue authority in whose area the hydrant was situated, namely **(..SPECIFY AUTHORITY..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 43(4) and (5) of the Fire and Rescue Services Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a person who proposed to carry out works for the purpose of supplying water to any part of the area of a fire and rescue authority
without reasonable excuse
failed to give at least 6 weeks' notice in writing to the authority OR
being a person who proposed to carry out works affecting a fire hydrant
without reasonable excuse
failed to give at least 7 days' notice in writing to the fire and rescue authority in whose area the hydrant is situated

english.standardstatementoffacts:

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 monthsOn the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
